item.title: Enhancing Spatiotemporal InSAR Retrieval of Snow Water Equivalent Using Multichannel and MAP Estimators
item.description: Differential repeat-pass interferometric synthetic aperture radar (d-InSAR) is an emerging method for retrieving seasonal snow water equivalent (SWE). The technique presents several limitations and sources of uncertainty related to decorrelation and phase ambiguities. For this reason, low-frequency bands are commonly preferred as they offer greater unambiguous retrieval ranges and coherence conservation. However, they lack sensitivity to small changes in snow mass due to long wavelengths. High-frequency bands provide higher sensitivity but suffer from decorrelation and phase wrapping under heavy snow accumulation. Future SAR satellite missions may enable simultaneous acquisitions. MultiChannel (MCh) techniques leverage the combination of statistically independent measurements to reduce noise and ambiguities. This study formulates MCh techniques for retrieving changes in SWE ( $\Delta \mathrm {SWE}$ ) using d-InSAR. Three MCh configurations were evaluated: L- and S-, L- and C-, and C- and X-bands. The theoretical performance was analyzed using the Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB). Experimental validation employed SodSAR, a 1–10 GHz tower-based SAR system, and compared single-band and MCh retrievals of $\Delta \mathrm {SWE}$ against in situ snow scale measurements. Additionally, semisynthetic simulations based on ALOS-2 data and a numerical snow model are provided for assessing distributed retrievals employing spatial filtering and Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) estimates. Results demonstrate that MCh configurations have the potential to improve retrieval accuracy, reduce noise, and resolve phase ambiguities.
item.authors: Jorge Jorge-Ruiz;Manu Holmberg;Juha Lemmetyinen;Ioanna Merkouriadi;Anna Kontu;Jouni Pulliainen;Jaan Praks;

item.title: The Neuro-Physical Inverter: A Modular Framework for Magnetotelluric Inversion Coupling Ensemble Conditioning With Residual Learning
item.description: We present the neuro-physical inverter (NPI), a modular, uncertainty-aware framework for geophysical inversion that couples ensemble-based conditioning with constrained residual learning, demonstrated in the 1-D magnetotelluric (MT) setting as a controlled testbed. The framework operates in two stages. An Ensemble-Conditional Gaussian Process (EnsCGP) conditions a prior ensemble of resistivity models on the observed response, producing a physically admissible reference ensemble. A residual-learning neural network then predicts targeted corrections to this reference, trained on synthetic data and fine-tuned per station for field application through a physics-coupled objective. Because an ensemble is conditioned, refined, and propagated through both stages, every estimate carries an associated ensemble spread. Synthetic experiments show that NPI systematically reduces ensemble-mean error without destabilizing the ensemble. Applied to broadband MT data from the Gabbs Valley geothermal region (Nevada, USA), NPI reduces the across-station mean misfit over the mid-period band while retaining comparable ensemble spread. The propagated ensemble yields a factor of uncertainty that serves as an operational measure of constraint within the assumed model class. Both stages are dimension-agnostic in formulation, and the design principles established here are intended to scale to higher-dimensional parameterizations.
item.authors: Jae Deok Kim;Sai Ravela;Rob. L. Evans;

item.title: Rethinking Multilabel Remote Sensing Image Classification Under Dual-Distribution Instance-Dependent Noise
item.description: Multilabel scene classification (MLC) is a fundamental task in remote sensing (RS). However, its performance is often limited by noisy annotations, where subtractive noise occurs when inconspicuous targets are missed and additive noise arises when visually confusing categories are falsely added. To simulate such annotation errors, the recently proposed instance-dependent multilabel noise (IDMN) method introduces the first instance-dependent noise generation strategy for RS MLC, driven by the intuition that hard label instances are more susceptible to mislabeling. Specifically, it leverages a single probability distribution of present labels to derive thresholds for both subtractive and additive noise generation. This design determines additive noise by requiring absent-label occurrence probabilities to exceed an irrelevant present-label threshold, leaving its quantity difficult to control and overlooking potentially confusing absent labels. To address this limitation, we propose dual-distribution IDMN (DD-IDMN), which explicitly decouples the score distributions of present and absent labels for calibrated noise generation. Empirical analysis under DD-IDMN reveals that additive noise yields more severe performance degradation than subtractive noise. To combat this DD-IDMN challenge, we propose the prompt-guided activation interference rectification network (PAIR-Net). Through cross-modal attention with learnable text prompts, it learns more discriminative RS feature representations. Furthermore, we introduce an activation-aware dynamic filtering (ADF) module to identify unreliable present labels for suppressing the more destructive additive noise under DD-IDMN. Experiments on UCMerced, AID, and MLRSNet demonstrate that PAIR-Net consistently outperforms representative noise-robust multilabel methods under complex instance-dependent noise. Our code is available at https://github.com/BasilLeave/PAIR-Net
item.authors: Xinlei Zhang;Fan Liu;Chuanyi Zhang;Xiaoying Ji;Wenhui Wang;Wei Zhou;Jun Zhou;

item.title: SegTrans-Diff: A Segmented Spatiotemporal Transformer With Echo-Aware Diffusion Refinement for Long-Lead Radar Echo Extrapolation
item.description: Accurate long-lead radar echo extrapolation is important for severe convective weather warning, but existing models suffer from echo displacement, intensity decay, and spatial blurring, weakening high-intensity echo detection and hazard-warning effectiveness. These difficulties arise because location-critical mesoscale evolution and uncertain convective-scale details require different modeling mechanisms. Deterministic models provide more reliable echo positions but tend to produce over-smoothed forecasts, whereas generative models can recover sharper structures but may introduce positional uncertainty or spurious echoes when weakly constrained by historical echo evolution. We propose SegTrans-Diff, a framework that decomposes 0–3-h extrapolation into segmented deterministic forecasting and echo-aware diffusion refinement. SegTrans predicts echo segments under segmented temporal encoding (STE), transforming asymmetric short-input long-output forecasting into segment-wise subtasks. Its SegTrans-Block combines window-wise global attention (WWGA) and frequency-wise temporal modeling (FWTM) to capture mesoscale organization and long-horizon temporal evolution. Built upon this location-aware forecast, the diffusion branch refines convective-scale details rather than generating echoes independently. The SegTrans forecast provides echo coverage, motion path, and mesoscale morphology, while encoder-derived spatiotemporal context (STC) carries historical echo-evolution information into denoising. Echo-aware gated spectral feature refinement (EG-SFR) uses forecast-derived echo and boundary gates to guide spectral feature refinement during denoising. Experiments on Shanghai radar echo dataset show that SegTrans achieves the highest pixel-wise critical success index (CSI) and Heidke skill score (HSS) among the compared models, while SegTrans-Diff improves neighborhood-based strong-echo forecast skill. Compared with DiffCast, SegTrans-Diff reduces the Fréchet inception distance (FID) by 42.8%.
item.authors: Fangli Wu;Huantong Geng;Jinzhong Min;Zhanpeng Shi;Shaoqiang Ma;

item.title: GLRF: Underwater Image Enhancement via Global and Local Visual Reconstruction Fusion
item.description: Underwater images frequently suffer from severe quality degradation caused by complex environmental conditions and the scattering and absorption of light during transmission, which greatly restricts their utility in subsequent analysis and applications. To tackle this challenge, this article presents an underwater image enhancement method that converges global and local visual reconstruction fusion to improve image quality and accuracy of visual tasks, called GLRF. Specifically, we first implement global color correction using the attenuated channel compensation strategy and correct local color bias using the local overlap-weighted color compensation strategy. Subsequently, we propose a structure-constrained luminance reconstruction method with smooth brightness transitions and gradient constraints for global contrast enhancement, which reduces noise caused by uneven brightness and preserves image details, while traditional histogram-based methods may introduce noise and cause irreversible detail loss when adjusting the brightness distribution. Ultimately, we exploit wavelet decomposition and reconstruction to unsharp mask the low-frequency components and adaptively threshold denoise the high-frequency components to reconstruct a high-visibility result. The comprehensive experiments on four benchmark datasets have shown that our GLRF achieves competitive or superior performance on most evaluated metrics. Additionally, the results of our GLRF enhancement are beneficial for feature matching.
item.authors: Ling Zhou;Hengyu Li;Peixian Zhuang;Weidong Zhang;

item.title: AAFNet: An Asymmetric Feature Encoding and Active Energy Modulation Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Forest Fire Detection
item.description: Forest fires pose severe ecological threats, yet dedicated multimodal architectures for such complex environments remain largely underexplored. Generic multimodal methods struggle to decouple heterogeneous physical properties, resist feature contamination during dynamic fusion, and preserve the fragile boundaries of microfires against deep semantic smoothing. To address these limitations, we propose an asymmetric feature encoding and active energy modulation network (AAFNet) for multimodal remote sensing forest fire detection. First, an asymmetric feature encoding is designed at the source. Within this architecture, the geometry-aware anchor (GAA) module is proposed to adaptively fit the nonrigid boundaries of smoke via decoupled deformable sampling. In parallel, the thermal-aware salient (TAS) module performs hierarchical wide-range perception operators to capture long-range thermal gradients and suppress radiation artifacts. Second, an energy-guided modulation (EGM) mechanism is formulated to dynamically allocate modality weights by quantifying instantaneous energy responses. This active regulation suppresses background interference and improves feature purity during fusion. Third, a decoupled difference reconstruction (DDR) unit is developed to explicitly reconstruct residual differences between adjacent feature hierarchies. This compensation maximizes the preservation of fine-grained textures for early stage fires. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our approach. The proposed model achieves an mAP@50 of 75.2%, an mAP@50–95 of 52.1% on forest fire datasets with only 2.531 M parameters, which comprehensively outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both detection accuracy and deployment parameters. Moreover, cross-dataset evaluation further demonstrates the generalization capability of AAFNet under diverse environmental distributions.
item.authors: Qinwen Li;Haiyan Li;Fuhua Ge;Pengfei Yu;Guanbo Wang;Xiang Liu;Yitong Fu;Jinde Cao;

item.title: Bridging the Gap of Missing Modalities: Common-Specific Knowledge Learning Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification
item.description: Multimodal learning has attracted significant attention in the field of remote sensing image classification due to its superior performance. Although multimodal data are often available during training, certain modalities may be unavailable during inference in real-world applications, posing a risk of performance degradation. To this end, we propose a novel common-specific knowledge learning network (CSKLNet) to bridge the gap of missing modalities. CSKLNet consists of two learning stages. First, complete multimodal knowledge is distilled from the teacher into the student under missing modalities, with the Wasserstein distance adopted to alleviate representation heterogeneity by minimizing feature distribution discrepancies. Second, two parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapters are inserted into the distilled student model to further exploit specific information from the available modalities. Compared with existing methods, CSKLNet not only inherits the common information from complete modalities but also fully leverages the available modality-specific information, thereby maintaining robust performance with missing modalities. Extensive experiments conducted on four distinct datasets indicate the advanced performance of the proposed method compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, with overall accuracy (OA) improvements of 1.34%–13.34%, 0.35%–3.54%, 0.55%–17.65%, and 0.17%–11.91% for hyperspectral image (HSI)–light detection and ranging (LiDAR) Houston2013, Trento, HSI–multispectral (MS) Houston2013, and QAI-Mangrove, respectively. The source code will be available at: https://github.com/ZhaohuiXue/CSKLNet
item.authors: Simin Zhu;Zhaohui Xue;Hao Wu;

item.title: ER-Net: Evolutionary Refinement Architecture With Spectral Purification for Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small target detection (ISTD) remains challenging because extremely weak target signals are often submerged in strong, nonstationary background clutter. Although deep-learning methods have advanced considerably, many architectures exhibit approximately isotropic low-pass behavior, causing irreversible attenuation of the high-frequency details of dim targets in deep layers. This article proposes an evolutionary refinement network (ER-Net), a detection framework that mitigates information dissipation through recursive feature refinement. Its central contribution is an asymmetric enhancement path: instead of using a conventional symmetric architecture, ER-Net treats the raw infrared (IR) image as an independent reference stream that bypasses shallow sampling and enters the deep hub directly, thereby supplying prior guidance at the most information-sensitive levels. First, a spectral purification module (SPM) performs adaptive feature cleaning in the frequency domain to suppress background noise while enhancing target-salient responses. Second, an evolutionary refinement hub (ER-Hub) uses global statistical fingerprints of the raw image to control feature evolution dynamically. The hub combines an Evolutionary Refinement Unit (ERU), which progressively strengthens and concentrates weak-target responses through recursive refinement, with residual synergistic fusion (RSF), which corrects residual errors and compensates for signal loss in nonlinear mappings. Extensive experiments on Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics (NUAA)-single-frame infrared small target (SIRST), National University of Defense Technology (NUDT)-SIRST, and infrared small target detection (IRSTD)-1K show that ER-Net achieves a competitive overall balance in pixel-level localization and background suppression. With a lightweight parameter count and high desktop inference efficiency, ER-Net provides an architecture–performance trade-off suitable for efficient IR detection in complex scenes. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/LXJK123/ER-Net.git
item.authors: Sheng-Yu Dai;Jian-Hua Qin;Zhong Liu;Hong-Wang Zhao;Xue-Qin Zhao;Ting-Ting Huang;

item.title: Wideband RFI Mitigation for Spaceborne SAR by Acquiring Prior Information via Time–Frequency Analysis
item.description: Operating in shared frequency bands, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) faces a complex electromagnetic environment, making radio frequency interference (RFI), particularly wideband interference (WBI), an increasingly prominent issue. WBI typically exhibits time-varying characteristics across pulses, with its amplitude and temporal location varying significantly. Despite these variations, WBI originating from the same source generally maintains stable intrinsic properties, such as bandwidth and duration, which can serve as useful prior information for WBI mitigation. However, due to the difficulty of WBI modeling, existing mitigation methods often bypass WBI parameter extraction, neglecting the utilization of prior information. Furthermore, these methods typically apply fixed filtering strategies across the entire WBI-containing pulse, ignoring variations in scattering intensity across different terrains. This leads to degraded mitigation performance in complex scenes. To address these issues, a WBI mitigation method that acquires prior information is proposed in this article. Specifically, through time–frequency analysis, WBI prior information is extracted from representative pulses identified via a spectral flatness indicator. WBI localization can be achieved by independently clustering strong- and weak-scattering regions, further optimized by the prior information. Finally, the eigen-subspace projection (ESP) method is applied to the localized time–frequency regions to mitigate WBI. Comprehensive experimental results on SAR data from diverse scenes confirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.
item.authors: Zijun Li;Zongsen Lv;Yanyang Liu;Ning Li;Lei Cui;

item.title: EFAWDet: Efficient Frequency-Role Assigned Wavelet-State-Space Fusion for RGB–Infrared Object Detection
item.description: Red, green, and blue (RGB)–infrared (IR) object detection leverages complementary visible texture and thermal cues to improve robustness under challenging conditions. However, existing feature-level fusion methods lack explicit frequency-role assignment: low-frequency semantic structures and high-frequency localization details are indiscriminately processed, squandering computation on redundant responses while suppressing the edge cues essential for precise localization. Moreover, global modeling operators such as Transformers and state-space models are uniformly applied to all frequency components, further degrading small-object boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight frequency-decoupled framework, namely efficient RGB-infrared detector (EFAWDet) that explicitly allocates distinct frequency bands to distinct detection functions. In EFAWDet, a multigroup wavelet fusion (MGWF) module decomposes dual-modal features and routes compact low-frequency components, which encode stable target-body semantics, to grouped cross-modal fusion. Then, a multigroup noncausal state-space duality (NC-SSD) performs noncausal global interaction confined within these reduced-resolution channel groups. Significantly, the separated RGB/IR high-frequency subbands are first adaptively fused through lightweight attention, then cached and reintroduced at the enhanced detection head (EDH) through inverse wavelet reconstruction as delayed localization compensation. This “low-frequency global modeling, high-frequency delayed compensation” strategy aligns the spectral properties of IR imagery with the frequency bias of state-space modeling, simultaneously reducing redundancy and preserving fine-grained localization cues. Extensive experiments on M3FD, LLVIP, forward-looking infrared (FLIR)-aligned, and DroneVehicle demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. EFAWDet-nano achieves 87.6% mAP50 and 58.7% mean average precision (mAP) on M3FD with only 2.5 M parameters and 16.5 GFLOPs (209.0 FPS), yielding a 99.1% reduction in parameter count compared to the YOLOv8-based FusionMamba while sacrificing merely 0.1 percentage point in mAP. The source code will be available at https://github.com/chenHeaven/EFAWDet
item.authors: Zhenghua Huang;Haiwen Chen;Qian Li;Yaozong Zhang;Chunhua Deng;Xin Xu;

item.title: Physics-Informed Blind Deconvolution for Seismic Resolution Enhancement Based on Zero-Shot Learning
item.description: The limited seismic resolution significantly degrades thin beds identification and reservoir characterization. Conventional deconvolution methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, while supervised deep learning (DL) methods require extensive high-fidelity labels. Although some unsupervised methods reduce the dependence on labels, they often lack geophysical interpretability. In addition, most DL-based deconvolution methods assume a known wavelet, which limits their applicability in practical scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed blind deconvolution workflow for seismic resolution enhancement based on zero-shot learning. Specifically, a three-stage progressive optimization strategy is proposed. An initial wavelet is first estimated by amplitude spectrum constraints and phase scanning. A dual-stream time–frequency network (DSTFNet) is then warmed up with the wavelet fixed to obtain a reliable initial reflectivity. Finally, the wavelet and the network parameters are alternately updated to achieve joint refinement of the wavelet and the reflectivity. In addition, we construct a joint loss function consisting of a physics-constrained Huber loss, and an L1 sparsity loss, which enhances physical interpretability and robustness to noise. Experiments on synthetic and field data demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits strong generalization and robustness.
item.authors: Wenshuo Yu;Shiqi Dong;Hongyuan Yang;Xintong Dong;

item.title: Multimodal Text-to-Set Remote Sensing Image Generation With Anchor Diffusion
item.description: Multimodal remote sensing imagery provides complementary information for Earth observation, yet acquiring large-scale, spatially aligned multimodal data is expensive and labor-intensive, motivating data-efficient multimodal image generation. Existing methods are primarily developed for single-modal synthesis or pairwise cross-modal generation and thus cannot explicitly model the scene structure shared by multiple modalities for multimodal set generation. This limitation makes it difficult to simultaneously preserve cross-modal spatial alignment and modality-specific fidelity. To address these issues, we propose anchor diffusion (AnchorDiff), a unified framework that is able to generate spatially aligned multimodal remote sensing images from textual descriptions. To enable text-to-set generation and multimodal spatial alignment, the proposed framework produces an optical image from the given text, which is then used to construct a modality-shared scene anchor as an explicit structural prior. Specifically, we devise a UNet-based AnchorMap extractor to learn a modality-shared anchor map from modality-specific patterns to constrain structural consistency across modalities. For the multimodal generative network, we implement a conditional diffusion with a structure–attention hybrid sampling (SA-Hybrid) strategy that integrates anchor-based structural control and reference-attention guidance, thus enhancing structural alignment while maintaining modality-specific fidelity. Experiments on benchmarks covering optical, multispectral, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and digital elevation model (DEM) data show that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of both spatial alignment and modality-specific fidelity. Code will be available at https://github.com/kyh433/Anchor-Diff
item.authors: Yuhan Kang;Honghu Pan;Hao Liu;Qiang Liu;Weiying Xie;Leyuan Fang;Lorenzo Bruzzone;

item.title: Bidirectional Entity Coupling Alignment for Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
item.description: Due to the homogeneous backgrounds and cluttered layouts of remote sensing (RS) imagery, fine-grained local entities are indispensable for preventing cross-modal semantic mismatch. However, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods based on contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) encapsulate scenes into holistic global representations, diluting these critical local cues. To address this, we propose the bidirectional entity-level alignment network (BEAN), a unified fine-grained entity alignment paradigm. First, to avoid the semantic ambiguity of conventional extraction mechanisms, we introduce a symmetric visual and textual entity construction paradigm comprising a visual entity bank constructor (VEBC) and a noun-to-token index constructor (NTIC). Specifically, VEBC constructs a visual entity bank via layerwise extraction, while NTIC performs index-guided extraction of textual entity embeddings, jointly delivering semantically discriminative cross-modal entity pairs. Second, to counteract the submersion of local entities within global embeddings, we design the cross-modal entity-bidirectional adapter (CEBA). It drives bidirectional cross-attention between the global feature stream and localized entity tokens. This mutually enriches isolated entities with holistic scene context, while simultaneously reinjecting fine-grained entity cues back into the global representations, effectively reversing the dilution process. Third, to overcome the absence of explicit entity-level supervision in traditional global contrastive objectives, we propose the fine-grained entity contrastive loss, a sample-level formulation that provides direct supervision for explicit entity alignment without requiring manual positive–negative pair annotation. Experiments on RSITMD, RSICD, and UCM-Captions datasets demonstrate that BEAN achieves leading mR scores of 50.74%, 34.67%, and 60.56%, respectively, consistently outperforming both PEFT-based methods and the fully fine-tuned CLIP baseline across all three benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/JasonGravity/BEAN
item.authors: Mengru Ma;Jiaxu Guo;Wenping Ma;Licheng Jiao;Yuting Yang;Xu Liu;Lingling Li;Fang Liu;

item.title: SSLANet: A Frequency–Spatial Visual System for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Hyperspectral image classification requires a compact representation that can jointly capture discriminative spectral cues, local spatial structures, and efficient inference behavior under limited annotations. Existing CNN-based methods provide effective local pattern extraction but are less capable of modeling long-range spectral dependencies. Transformer-based models improve global interaction at the cost of considerable computational overhead, whereas recent state-space models usually formulate hyperspectral data as spatial–spectral sequences and still leave transform-domain spectral variations insufficiently explored. To address these limitations, we propose a spectral–spatial learning adaptive network (SSLANet), an efficient frequency–spatial learning network for hyperspectral image classification. The core component is a residual frequency–spatial layer that integrates an adaptive spectral block (ASB) and an interactive convolution block (ICB). ASB performs learnable complex-valued spectral modulation together with input-dependent frequency-energy selection to enhance material-sensitive spectral responses, while ICB propagates the filtered features into local neighborhoods through multiplicative spatial–channel interaction. This design differs from fixed transform-domain preprocessing in that the frequency response is conditioned on the current input feature distribution through a soft mask and an effective transfer function in the latent frequency domain. Extensive experiments on three public hyperspectral benchmarks demonstrate that SSLANet achieves competitive classification accuracy with favorable computational efficiency. The source code is available at https://github.com/NELUJA86/SSLANet
item.authors: Xiaofei Yang;Ruiying Zhang;Weijia Cao;Jiangtao Peng;Yifang Ban;Yicong Zhou;

item.title: SDMCNet: Spatial–Spectral Decoupled Mamba–MoE Collaborative Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Using the whole image as input for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, the model needs to handle broader spatial dependencies and more diverse spectral variations. In modeling nonlocal spatial relationships, scanning based on fixed windows is prone to directional bias, leading to the loss of spatial boundary details. In addition, the high dimensionality of the data makes spectral distributions complex and spectral information redundant, thereby affecting the reliable identification and effective utilization of spectral bands. To address these challenges, we propose SDMCNet, a spatial–spectral decoupled Mamba–mixture-of-expert (MoE) collaborative network for image-level HSI classification. Taking the whole image as input, SDMCNet achieves a balance between spatial structure modeling and fine-grained spectral representation. Specifically, the spatial branch progressive spatial perception feature extraction (PSPFE) integrates local and global Mamba modules to capture short- and long-range spatial contextual dependencies. A boundary constrained enhancement module (BCEM) is further introduced to suppress oversmoothing and noisy perturbations near class boundaries, thereby preserving spatial boundary details. The spectral branch anchor routed expert spectral aggregation (ARESA) builds an anchor routed expert collaboration mechanism to adaptively select complementary spectral experts to model complex dependencies among spectral bands and obtain precise spectral band combinations. The two branches collaborate through spectral channel weighting, thereby achieving synergistic spatial–spectral modeling for image-level HSI classification. Extensive experiments on the Indian Pines (IP), Pavia University (PU), Houston 2013, and HanChuan (HC) datasets demonstrate that SDMCNet consistently outperforms representative methods, validating the effectiveness and potential value of using the whole image as input for HSI classification. The code is available at https://github.com/chai-xue/SDMCNet
item.authors: Xue Chai;Bingbing Lei;Wei Feng;Ruiqing Zhang;Zhipeng Liu;

item.title: Difference Approximation Network With Semantic Alignment for Remote Sensing Change Captioning
item.description: Remote sensing change captioning (RSCC) plays an important role in advancing remote sensing spatiotemporal understanding with vision-language generation. However, due to the temporal evolution of geospatial patterns, bitemporal images are susceptible to the influence of lighting conditions and seasonal effects. Existing methods fail to effectively utilize the cross-sample difference information and perform explicit multimodal alignment of key changes, which often results in inaccurate descriptions of changes in key objects and their relationships. To address these issues, the article proposes a novel difference approximation network with semantic alignment (DANSA) for RSCC. Specifically, a cross-temporal feature transform (CFT) is introduced to interact with feature representations extracted from the contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) model. Then, to learn a reliable difference representation, a difference memory approximation (DMA) is designed to enhance the difference representation of the current scene by activating difference information from training samples. Furthermore, considering that pretrained language embedding models can serve as a powerful supervisory signal, a change semantic alignment (CSA) is constructed to achieve fine-grained alignment between visual and textual features. In this way, DANSA generates comprehensive scene change captions that accurately depict objects and relationships across time. Extensive experiments and analyses conducted on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that DANSA achieves competitive performance with fewer training parameters. The code will be available at https://github.com/zcsisiyao/DANSA
item.authors: Cheng Zhang;Zhongle Ren;Biao Hou;Shijie Liu;Changhui Xu;Weibin Li;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: A Novel Image Change Detection Approach Based on Siamese Superpixel-Guided Graph Transformer
item.description: Change detection (CD) of very-high-resolution (HR) remote sensing (RS) images remains a challenging task due to complex spatial patterns and massive scale variations of land covers. Recently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Transformers have achieved remarkable progress in this field. However, since existing Transformers and graph-fused methods generally construct nodes on regular grids or pixels, which breaks the inherent structural consistency of objects and blurs fine boundaries, they still struggle to achieve an optimal balance between capturing long-range global contexts and preserving fine-grained local geometric details (e.g., sharp boundaries) under acceptable computational costs. To address these dilemmas, a novel Siamese superpixel-guided graph convolutional Transformer (SiamSGCT) for efficient and accurate CD is proposed in this article. Specifically, a superpixel-guided graph representation (SGR) module is investigated to project dense pixel-level features into a compact graph space, inherently maintaining the structural consistency of objects. Subsequently, a graph convolutional Transformer (GCT) is utilized to model coarse-to-fine object-level semantic dependencies within the graph domain. Furthermore, to bridge the semantic gap between different topological spaces, a cross-space pixel-graph fusion (CPGF) module is proposed to deeply inject the aggregated global graph contexts back into the dense pixel domain, achieving reciprocal enhancement. Finally, to mitigate the inevitable boundary aliasing effect during graph-to-pixel reprojection, a Laplacian boundary-aware optimization strategy is introduced, which explicitly forces the network to focus on high-frequency structural information for precise contour delineation. Experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets (LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and CLCD) demonstrate that the proposed SiamSGCT outperforms several state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving a superior tradeoff between detection accuracy and model complexity. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/maren/SiamSGCT
item.authors: Xiaochen Lu;Diman Xiao;Shenglan Wang;Jingjing Zhang;Yajun Li;

item.title: Robust Marine CSEM Signal Enhancement in Low-SNR Environments Using a Mixed Multistable Stochastic Pooling Network
item.description: The marine controlled-source electromagnetic (MCSEM) method is used to reconstruct deep subsurface resistivity distributions. However, low-frequency ambient noise and instrumental interference reduce the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of observed responses and degrade the stability of resistivity inversion. To address this noise-induced inversion degradation under low-SNR conditions, this study proposes a signal enhancement framework that integrates a mixed multistable stochastic resonance (MMSR) model with an adaptive stochastic pooling network (SPN). The MMSR model enhances the target-frequency components of MCSEM responses while suppressing uncorrelated noise. Parallel stochastic resonance (SR) nodes are constructed for multichannel signal fusion, allowing the framework to accommodate complex noise patterns. A recursive least squares (RLSs) algorithm is then used to adaptively optimize the pooling weights for further signal enhancement. Synthetic results show that the multistable SR–stochastic pooling network (MMSR-SPN) method improves the average SNR by 13.79 dB and maintains consistent enhancement performance under varying noise levels. Field datasets further validate its practical applicability. The processed time-series waveforms exhibit more pronounced attenuation and periodic features, attaining a spectrum improvement ratio (SIR) of 14.2. The magnitude-versus-offset (MVO) and phase-versus-offset (PVO) curves become smoother and more continuous, and the derived inversion results are consistent with known stratigraphic records. Numerical simulations and field-data experiments confirm that the proposed framework effectively alleviates noise-induced inversion instability, providing a robust signal enhancement solution for geophysical electromagnetic exploration.
item.authors: Yihan Tian;Wanyue Zhang;Fan Yang;Suyi Li;

item.title: How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain? Generalization Bounds for Spatially Dependent Data
item.description: Machine learning classifiers for remote sensing imagery are typically evaluated as though every pixel were an independent sample. Spatial autocorrelation violates this assumption, since neighboring pixels carry redundant information which inflates sample sizes. How many independent samples does a satellite image actually contain? For an $n \times n$ image whose spatial correlation persists over a range of $r$ pixels, the effective sample size is $\Theta (n^{2}/r^{2})$ , not $n^{2}$ . We prove this as a finite-sample upper bound for classifiers on spatially correlated data, and show via a matching lower bound that the rate is tight, and no algorithm can do better. We extend the results to images with directional correlation and spatially varying correlation structure. Our result justifies spatial cross-validation since block holdout with separation proportional to the correlation range achieves optimal generalization guarantees, while random holdout can underestimate confidence interval widths by a factor proportional to $r$ . We validate the theory on synthetic data and satellite image tiles from three sensors (Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-1).
item.authors: Robin Young;

item.title: MAPLE: Modality-Adaptive Prior-Guided Learning With Language-Conditioned Spatial Adaptation for Multimodal Remote Sensing Segmentation
item.description: Multimodal remote sensing segmentation benefits from complementary information across heterogeneous data sources, yet effectively leveraging such information while preserving the generalization ability of pretrained models remains challenging. In this article, we propose modality-adaptive prior-guided learning (MAPLE), a unified framework that adapts a frozen foundation backbone for multimodal learning via lightweight modality-aware mechanisms and language-guided priors. By introducing adaptive feature modulation and semantic guidance, the proposed approach effectively mitigates modality discrepancies and improves spatial prediction consistency. In addition, an adaptive reweighting strategy is employed to address class imbalance and enhance the learning of underrepresented categories. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that MAPLE achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with the smallest trainable footprint among the compared methods, while a comprehensive efficiency analysis of total parameters, floating-point operations (FLOPs), inference latency, and memory consumption further confirms a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. The source code is available at https://github.com/shiroSamaNanoda/MAPLE.git
item.authors: Qiao Sun;Zechao Hu;Lin Chen;Zerui Xiao;Shukan Liu;Hui Yang;Xianzhang Chen;

item.title: Reliability-Aware Spatiotemporal Consistency Regulation for Satellite Video Tracking
item.description: The satellite video single object tracking (SVSOT) remains challenging because low image quality and cluttered backgrounds yield unreliable target evidence. Although recent trackers have improved robustness by enhancing feature representations and cross-frame interactions, they lack regulation of the reliability of evidence used for recursive feature updates. As single object tracking (SOT) can be seen as a recursive process, once unreliable evidence is absorbed into the target state, it may bias subsequent associations, accumulate spatiotemporal inconsistency, and eventually cause tracking drift or failure. To tackle these issues, we propose SCRTrack, a spatiotemporal consistency regulation framework that regulates the formation of target evidence and its propagation and maintenance across frames. Specifically, a multilayer feature formation (MFF) module is proposed to inject shallow structural details into deep semantic representations, enhancing spatial discriminability while suppressing clutter-induced interference. A reliability-guided context propagation (RCP) module is further designed to estimate interframe correspondence reliability and uses it to modulate temporal state updates, reducing the impact of ambiguous associations on state evolution. In addition, a motion consistency preservation (MCP) mechanism is introduced to monitor motion-consistent response displacements under occlusion and similar-object interference, maintaining target identity when appearance-based evidence becomes unreliable. Extensive experiments on SatSOT, SV248S, and OOTB demonstrate that SCRTrack achieves the state-of-the-art performance and exhibits strong robustness across challenging satellite tracking scenarios.
item.authors: Xiaowen Zhang;Haijiang Sun;Hanqing Sun;Hongliang Chang;Xilai Wei;Chao Ma;

item.title: Retrieving Specific Differential Phase for Dual-Frequency Dual-Polarization Doppler Cloud Radar
item.description: The specific differential phase ( $K_{\text {DP}}$ ) is an indispensable polarimetric radar variable for investigating the microphysical properties of precipitation. Utilizing the differential propagation phase ( $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ ) identified by a Rayleigh plateau detection algorithm based on the differential reflectivity ( $Z_{\text {DR}}$ ) spectra, the reflectivity differential phase (ZPHI) approach is extended to retrieve $K_{\text {DP}}$ for a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) dual-frequency (one is at 35 GHz and the other is at 95 GHz) dual-polarization Doppler cloud radar. Three constraints are imposed on the ZPHI approach, including a range-partitioning scheme based on the fluctuation characteristics of $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ , a nonnegative constraint on the specific attenuation, and a convergence constraint to terminate the calculation. The $Z_{\text {DR}}$ and $\Phi _{\text {DP}}$ spectra during a stratiform precipitation event on February 3, 2021, and the raindrop size and distribution drop size and distribution (DSD) dataset collected by a disdrometer deployed in Cabauw, The Netherlands, are utilized to demonstrate its practical performance. The result shows that: 1) the ZPHI approach is effectively extended to retrieve $K_{\text {DP}}$ in dominant Mie scattering situations. Radar-retrieved $K_{\text {DP}}$ at both frequencies can be well derived with a high spatio-temporal resolution, and agree well with DSD-derived $K_{\text {DP}}$ across the precipitation event; 2) the combined use of $\delta _{\text {co}}$ , $V_{\text {R}}$ , and $K_{\text {DP}}$ can adequately describe the relevant microphysical characteristics for the stratiform precipitation event, which agrees well with the evolution of surface DSD-derived $D_{0}$ ; and 3) the impacts of short-duration DSD changes can be well captured by the fluctuated $K_{\text {DP}}$ and $\delta _{\text {co}}$ at both frequencies, and the drop shape ratio (DSR) changes explain the residual $K_{\text {DP}}$ deviations at Ka-band, as another potential response to DSD changes within radar range bins.
item.authors: Yabin Gou;Christine Unal;Herman Russchenburg;

item.title: Adaptive Calibration for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Coastal wetland hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) is practically constrained by scarce labeled samples. Cross-domain few-shot learning (CDFSL) provides a promising solution by enabling knowledge transfer under limited supervision. However, coastal wetlands exhibit high spectral similarity and spatial heterogeneity. Existing CDFSL methods struggle to disentangle such complex geomorphology, leading to insufficient feature discriminability. Furthermore, severe prototype estimation bias and domain shift persist as inherent challenges. To address these issues, an adaptive calibration strategy for CDFSL is proposed. Specifically, a collaborative perception feature extractor (CPFE) with a spectral–spatial adaptive differencing module (SSAD) and a dual-stream gated fusion module (DGFM) is constructed to extract the fine-grained signatures and complex spatial structures. Building upon these robust representations, we design a dynamic prototype interaction calibration (DPIC) module, which adaptively distinguishes typical samples from hard samples via the prediction confidence of query samples, thereby constructing and fusing multiple auxiliary prototypes to enable class prototypes to better approximate the latent data distribution. Finally, we develop a synergistic global domain alignment (SGDA) strategy that jointly aligns macroscopic spatial distributions and spectral baselines while preserving class-discriminative structures. Extensive experiments on three self-constructed hyperspectral image (HSI) datasets and one public dataset demonstrate the superiority of the proposed CDFSL method for HSIC via adaptive calibration (ACFSL).
item.authors: Zhongwei Li;Wenhui Peng;Qixing Yu;Fangming Guo;Guangbo Ren;Jianbu Wang;Xinchen Lu;

item.title: 3D-S2RNet: Reconstructing 3-D Radar Reflectivity Based on Himawari AHI Measurements
item.description: 3-D atmospheric hydrometeors measured by radars play crucial roles in hazardous weather, such as heavy rain, hail, and strong winds, but radars only cover very limited parts of the globe. This article develops a 3-D radar reflectivity reconstruction model, 3D-S2RNet, to retrieve high-resolution (1-km Horizontally and 0.5–1-km vertically) 3-D radar reflectivity with inputs from Japanese advanced Himawari imager (AHI, 16 channel) data. 3D-S2RNet integrates a conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN), 2-D/3-D attention mechanisms, and a weighted composite loss strategy to retrieve the structural details of 3-D radar reflectivity, resolving the oversmoothing issue in existing methods. 3D-S2RNet significantly outperforms the baseline U-Net model across all key metrics, achieving a nearly fivefold improvement in critical success index (CSI) for retrieving intense radar reflectivity cores ( $\ge $ 45 dBZ). It accurately reconstructs diverse weather systems, including squall lines, typhoons, frontal systems, and low-latitude rain clusters. This work provides a novel capability to retrieve 3-D radar reflectivity from geostationary satellite imager observations, which has great potential to support cloud-sensitive applications, including numerical weather prediction (NWP) initialization, severe weather nowcasting, solar energy prediction, and aviation weather forecasting.
item.authors: Yu Qin;Yubao Liu;Xuan Wang;Qinqing Xiong;Jing Duan;

item.title: HydroDrone: A Circular External-Looking UAV-SAR Campaign for Short-Term Temporal Decorrelation Characterization
item.description: This article presents the HydroDrone campaign, a dedicated uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) experiment designed to characterize short-term temporal decorrelation over vegetated scenes. The system employs a C-band frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar mounted on a multirotor UAV, performing repeated circular external-looking acquisitions over a chosen test site. This configuration enables the generation of dense interferometric stacks with temporal baselines ranging from tens of seconds to several hours. This work derives the specific mathematical framework for the computation of along-track wavenumbers and azimuth resolution in circular external-looking geometries, highlighting the fundamental differences with respect to standard linear trajectories. To compensate for residual trajectory errors arising from navigation uncertainties, a multiaperture interferometric trajectory compensation algorithm is introduced and applied across the stack. Preliminary results from a single campaign day are presented, including interferometric phase and coherence stacks before and after trajectory compensation. Coherence matrices computed over three different land-cover types (cornfield, medium-height vegetation, and meadow) are analyzed as a preliminary assessment of the coherence behavior and temporal sampling capability of the HydroDrone system. Thermal and spatial decorrelation contributions are quantified to confirm that the observed coherence loss is primarily driven by temporal decorrelation, providing a robust experimental basis for future vegetation clutter decorrelation modeling.
item.authors: Pietro Grassi;Marco Manzoni;Stefano Moro;Andrea Monti-Guarnieri;Julia Kubanek;Stefano Tebaldini;

item.title: HMMamba: A Heterogeneous Multibranch Mamba Architecture for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is crucial for applications like precision agriculture and urban planning, necessitating the effective integration of spatial and spectral features. However, existing methods often struggle with limited receptive fields, structural damage from data transformation, or high computational complexity, hindering an optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency. To tackle these challenges, we propose HMMamba—a lightweight, accurate, and interpretable heterogeneous multibranch architecture (HMBA). Its core innovation lies in our first proposal of the structured Mamba modeler (SMM), which sequences and reconstructs high-dimensional data through structure-preserving axial compaction and recombination, employing an orientation-separated shared Mamba mechanism to efficiently achieve global dependency modeling. The framework is further augmented by a lightweight anisotropy perceiver (AP) for mid-range spatial structures and a detail enhancer (DE) for local discriminative features. These three complementary branches collectively construct a comprehensive multiscale feature hierarchy. Extensive experiments on five public HSI datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a top overall accuracy (OA) of 98.26%, with merely 0.44 M parameters and an inference speed of 0.01 s, significantly outperforming current convolutional neural network (CNN)-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based models. Experimental results and visualization analyses show that HMMamba excels in structural integrity, classification accuracy, computational efficiency, and interpretability, positioning it as a promising next-generation HSI classifier. The code for this work will be available at https://github.com/IIPGroup-C/HMMamba
item.authors: Yongchao Sun;Jing Wang;Tongzhen Si;Tao Xu;Guangqi Li;Xiaohui Yang;

item.title: Multigranularity Selective Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models for Coastal Remote Sensing Scene Classification
item.description: Large-scale coastal reclamation activities in recent decades have had a significant impact on the sustainability of marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) plays a critical role in environmental monitoring and marine management; however, existing RSSC techniques are underdeveloped for coastal regions, especially in the study of intraclass and interclass properties among different types of coastal remote sensing images. A benchmark dataset dedicated to coastal scene interpretation is crucially missing. To address this gap, we construct a new coastal remote sensing scene dataset, termed CROSS-14, which contains 3925 images spanning 14 representative coastal use patterns. To effectively handle the complex heterogeneity of coastal scenes, we propose a multigranularity selective fine-tuning (MGSF) framework to adapt vision foundation models (VFMs) for classifying coastal remote sensing images. MGSF adopts a progressive classification network consisting of linear probing and selective fine-tuning. At the sample granularity level, an uncertainty-aware reweighting (UAR) strategy is designed to emphasize difficult and ambiguous samples based on linear probing results. At the feature level, dual-selective adapters (DSA) are introduced to adaptively select informative tokens and channels while suppressing redundant representations. Extensive experiments conducted on CROSS-14 and two public benchmarks under various settings demonstrate that MGSF achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/wangxinlu-y/MGSF
item.authors: Kai Zhang;Xinlu Wang;Feng Zhang;Lifeng Wang;Jiande Sun;Sen-Ching Samson Cheung;

item.title: An Entropy-Driven Optimization Framework for Sustainable Remote Sensing Onboard Processing in Energy-Constrained LEO Networks
item.description: High-resolution remote sensing (HRS) missions generate large onboard imagery streams that must be transformed into timely HRS products or alerts. Direct downlink of raw RS data or fully local onboard processing is difficult for energy-constrained low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites because sensing, intersatellite transmission, computation, and downlink operations jointly stress battery depth of discharge (DoD) and thermal safety. In this article, we formulate a communication–sensing–computation coordination problem for sustainable onboard HRS processing in energy-constrained LEO networks. To solve it efficiently, we propose an entropy-based edge computing (EEC) framework that decomposes the problem into two stages: entropy-driven multiedge-LEO selection and sequential closed-form resource allocation. To support timely onboard HRS product generation, we propose a multiedge offloading model in which the sensing LEO uses its four laser intersatellite link (LISL) terminals to simultaneously offload up to four RS processing task instances to distinct edge satellites selected by the entropy-driven scoring stage. The second stage determines the minimum feasible adjustable LISL power required to sustain stable high-rate permanent-LISL offloading and then derives closed-form updates for sensing and computing frequencies while respecting energy, thermal, and delay limits. Simulations under a disaster-monitoring HRS processing workload demonstrate that EEC enables timely onboard HRS product generation by maintaining low mission-deadline violations, limiting the sensing-LEO DoD to about 21%, preserving thermal safety, and improving timely HRS product-generation reliability to about 94.2% compared with the considered baselines.
item.authors: Ahmad Y. Alhusenat;Lei Lei;Qizhou Wang;Hana Rababah;Xingjun Zhang;Xiangyong Cao;Symeon Chatzinotas;

item.title: LAGF-FracNet: Liquid ODE-Driven Adaptive Graph Fusion for Fine-Grained Geological Body Segmentation in Borehole Electrical Images
item.description: In borehole-scale geophysical remote sensing, electrical imaging logging actively acquires subsurface electrical responses and provides millimeter-scale borehole wall texture information for identifying geological bodies such as fractures and bedding. However, accurate pixel-wise segmentation of such borehole imaging data remains challenging. The difficulty arises from the elongated morphology, weak boundaries, sparse spatial distribution of fracture- and bedding-related targets, as well as pseudo-responses induced by complex borehole conditions and cross-well distribution shifts. To address these issues, this study proposes, namely the liquid ODE-driven adaptive graph fusion fracture network (LAGF-FracNet), a dual-branch deep learning framework for geological body segmentation in borehole electrical imaging logs. The framework integrates a convolutional neural network and a Swin Transformer (Swin-T) to jointly model local textural details and global structural semantics. Furthermore, continuous feature evolution, cross-branch alignment, adaptive graph fusion, and tri-decoder joint supervision are introduced to enhance structural representation, heterogeneous feature interaction, and decoding consistency. The proposed framework is designed for intelligent interpretation of borehole-scale remote sensing images under complex subsurface imaging conditions, aiming to improve the automated segmentation and characterization of fractures and bedding-related structures for logging interpretation and reservoir evaluation. The method was validated on two datasets, namely EIL-I and EIL-II. EIL-I is an in-house dataset constructed from 21 wells in the Sichuan Basin, whereas EIL-II is a public dataset derived from the Utah FORGE project. On EIL-I, LAGF-FracNet achieves 98.24% precision, 89.76% recall, 93.81% $F1$ -score, 86.98% mean intersection over union (mIoU), and 97.76% mean pixel accuracy (mPA). On EIL-II, it obtains 91.63% precision, 89.25% recall, 90.42% $F1$ -score, 85.16% mIoU, and 93.61% mPA. Experimental results demonstrate that LAGF-FracNet effectively preserves structural continuity, suppresses pseudo-responses, and maintains consistent performance across the two evaluated datasets, indicating its potential for borehole-scale remote sensing interpretation and reservoir evaluation.
item.authors: Huazhong Yang;Zhiliang Zhang;Jiahui Zhang;Liu Jun;Chong Zhang;

item.title: Natural Fracture Identification From Conventional Well Logs Using Geology-Aware Relative Anomaly Representation and Anchor-Constrained Interval Decoding
item.description: Reliable identification of natural fractures from conventional well logs is complicated by nonunique fracture signatures under lithofacies heterogeneity and interwell baseline drift. Pointwise classifiers tend to fragment fracture zones, whereas unconstrained sequence models may overextend them. Depth-wise autocorrelation further complicates performance evaluation by producing overly optimistic estimates. We propose geology-aware interval decoding (GAID) to address these limitations through two methodological advances and a leakage-aware evaluation design. First, a geology-background-conditioned representation expresses fracture-sensitive responses as local deviations while incorporating multilog consistency and stratigraphic context, thereby improving response comparability across wells. Second, candidate-anchor-constrained decoding separates pointwise candidate localization from contextual assessment and permits interval expansion only within finite neighborhoods of candidate anchors, limiting boundary drift and error propagation. Evaluation combines leave-one-well-out (LOWO) testing, an independently held-out well, spatial-separation audits, and strict, depth-tolerant, and event-level metrics. Under threefold LOWO validation, GAID achieved well-averaged strict and ±0.25-m-tolerant $F1$ scores of 75.60% and 85.39%, respectively. These exceeded the strongest deep-learning baseline by 3.57 and 3.32 percentage points, respectively. Random pointwise splitting yielded a strict $F1$ score 12.45 percentage points higher than LOWO validation, highlighting the sensitivity of performance estimates to the validation protocol. GAID achieved a ±0.25-m-tolerant $F1$ score of 88.12% on a predesignated held-out shale well. On a held-out tight-sandstone well, it achieved a strict $F1$ score of 75.27% after target-domain retraining. These results support GAID as a structured and leakage-aware workflow for cross-well fracture identification, without implying zero-shot cross-lithology transfer.
item.authors: Shiqiang Liu;Lianbo Zeng;Jiarui Zhang;Xiaoyu Du;Baoyu Liang;Zhen Wang;

item.title: 2DTS-MixNet: A Lightweight Mixing Network for Efficient Crop Classification Across Diverse Cropping Systems
item.description: Accurate and timely crop type classification is essential for agricultural monitoring, food security assessment, and agricultural policy making. As crop mapping is increasingly required to identify fine-grained crop types and complex cropping systems, dense satellite time series are needed to characterize subtle phenological differences and spectral variations among crop types. However, long and dense temporal observations substantially increase the computational burden, which limits the efficiency of large-scale crop classification. To address this, a lightweight mixing network, named 2-D temporal–spectral MixNet (2DTS-MixNet), is proposed for crop classification from satellite time series. Annual long time series are first transformed into a 2-D temporal–spectral (2DTS) representation, where temporal observations are arranged in a 2-D layout and spectral bands are stacked along the channel dimension. Local temporal–spectral patterns, long-range phenological dependencies, and cross-band interactions are then learned through nonoverlapping patch embedding, local/global temporal token mixing (GTTM), and spectral-channel mixing modules, respectively. The proposed method was evaluated in four typical cropping systems, including a 27-class complex crop classification scenario in the United States, a large-area crop classification scenario in France, fragmented smallholder fields in Kenya, and multiseason cropping systems in Brazil. The results showed that 2DTS-MixNet achieved the best average performance among the compared state-of-the-art methods, with an average overall accuracy (OA) of 66.89% across the four study areas. In terms of end-to-end mapping efficiency, the total time cost of the complete mapping workflow was reduced by up to approximately 37%. Overall, 2DTS-MixNet provides an efficient and scalable lightweight modeling method for crop classification from satellite time series, and can support large-scale crop mapping and rapid agricultural monitoring across diverse cropping systems.
item.authors: Hengbin Wang;Xinyue Li;Ruixiang Huo;Yuanyuan Zhao;Shaoming Li;Xiaodong Zhang;Zhe Liu;

item.title: Balancing Consistency and Generalization via Cross-Sample Memory Bank for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
item.description: Change detection (CD) is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis, aiming to identify changes between images acquired at different times. For CD, it is critical to learn the consistent features of unchanged regions across multitemporal images. However, forcing consistent features also impacts the representation of diverse scenarios, resulting in decayed generalization capability. In this article, we simultaneously consider the unchanged consistency and cross-scene generalization and propose a constraint and memory network (C-MNet). First, a dual-branch backbone integrating SAM2 and VMamba is constructed to model both spatial and cross-temporal dependencies simultaneously for better capturing the consistency. Then a mask-guided dual-temporal reconstruction module is designed which enforces cross-temporal reconstruction consistency on unchanged areas and enables the network to explicitly learn temporal invariance. However, consistency-driven reconstruction tends to suppress feature diversity in different scenarios, biasing the model toward dominant land-cover patterns. To overcome this limitation, we further design a cross-sample Memory Bank mechanism that stores stable unchanged features and serves as a historical reference during training. C-MNet effectively balances consistency constraints and feature diversity, leading to improved recognition capability of changed regions and cross-scene generalization. The code of this work can be found on https://github.com/4043-lab/Change-detection
item.authors: Xia Zhang;Jinyu Han;Jia Liu;Wenhua Zhang;Fang Liu;Liang Xiao;

item.title: DHMD: Harnessing the Power of State-Space Models for Advanced Vehicle-Aware RGB–T Object Detection in Spatial–Frequency Domain
item.description: Red-green-blue–thermal (RGB–T) multimodal object detection has become an effective paradigm for robust remote sensing perception by exploiting the complementary characteristics of visible (VI) and thermal imagery. However, existing convolutional neural network (CNN)- and Transformer-based RGB–T detectors still suffer from several limitations, including insufficient global context modeling or high computational cost, modality heterogeneity and cross-modal feature misalignment, inadequate spatial–frequency feature interaction, and weak perception of small vehicles in complex remote sensing scenes. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel dual-head Mamba detector (DHMD), an accuracy-oriented RGB–T detector that achieves a favorable tradeoff between detection accuracy and computational efficiency for remote sensing vehicle detection. The proposed method focuses on two fundamental aspects: cross-modal discrepancy modeling and task-aware vehicle representation. First, to address the semantic misalignment and spatial–frequency representation discrepancy between RGB and thermal modalities, DHMD establishes a unified cross-modal representation learning strategy. A dual-Mamba backbone is employed to efficiently capture long-range dependencies with linear computational complexity, while an align-fuse module for semantic flow (AFMSF) alleviates cross-modal semantic misalignment through bimodal semantic enhancement, learnable semantic flow field prediction, and deformable alignment-based feature fusion. Meanwhile, a space–frequency interactive mixer (SFIM) jointly models spatial structures and frequency-domain information to strengthen spatial–frequency feature coupling and enhance the representation of small vehicles. Second, to address the small-scale, densely distributed, and geometrically structured characteristics of remote sensing vehicles, a task-aware vehicle representation strategy is developed by incorporating vehicle-aware geometric priors into adaptive multiscale feature fusion through a rectangular self-adaptive calibration adaptive spatial feature fusion (RSC-ASFF) module, thereby improving the robustness of vehicle perception in complex scenes. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle, vehicle detection in aerial imagery (VEDAI), and M3FD datasets demonstrate that DHMD achieves state-of-the-art detection performance, obtaining mAP50 scores of 0.834, 0.679, and 0.848, respectively. These results validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed framework for red-green-blue–thermal (RGB–T) remote sensing vehicle detection.
item.authors: Chengrui Yu;Guangxin Li;Baolin Lv;Yuanhao Gong;Yao Fu;Yuyang Huang;Chang Yu;Xiaonan Jiang;

item.title: ReportsNet: Rotation-Enhanced Polar-Radial Topology Synergy Network for Hyperspectral and LiDAR-Derived DSM Joint Classification
item.description: Joint classification of hyperspectral (HS) imagery and light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-derived digital surface models (DSMs) commonly represents local neighborhoods on Cartesian grids, where changes in object orientation alter the spatial arrangement presented to the fusion network. Existing fusion architectures do not explicitly encode center-relative radial distances, cyclic angular relationships, or geometrically corresponding cross-modal locations. To address this gap, the rotation-enhanced polar-radial topology synergy network (ReportsNet) is proposed, which locally reorganizes co-registered HS and DSM patches into target-centered polar-radial representations and models complementary distance-based and relative-angle-aware context for multimodal fusion. On the MUUFL, Trento, and Houston datasets, ReportsNet obtains OAs of 91.99%, 99.45%, and 90.69%, respectively. It achieves the highest OA on all three datasets, exceeding the next-best compared methods by 1.44, 0.44, and 1.28 percentage points, respectively. In the Houston rotation experiment from 0° to 90°, ReportsNet yields an OA standard deviation of 0.06%, indicating stable performance under the evaluated perturbations. The code is available at https://github.com/LuyangLyu/radial-flow
item.authors: Luyang Lyu;Wenbo Yu;He Huang;Danfeng Hu;Liqiang Zhang;

item.title: From Pseudoclasses to Real Changes: Spatial–Spectral Difference Learning for Mitigating Spectral Pseudochange in Hyperspectral Change Detection
item.description: A core challenge in hyperspectral change detection (HCD) is spectral pseudochange, artifacts from imaging conditions that cause severe overlap between changed and unchanged samples, reducing their separability and hindering accurate detection. Existing methods, including traditional difference-driven pipelines and deep learning models, remain vulnerable to such discrepancies. To address this issue, we use pseudoclass separability as a design perspective to guide spatial–spectral representation enhancement, where changed and unchanged labels are regarded as discriminative surrogate categories defined on bitemporal spectral pairs rather than semantic land-cover categories. We propose spatial–spectral difference learning (SSDL), a spatial–spectral difference enhancement framework whose central component is spectral attention (SpeA) for peak-valley spectral-structure enhancement. SpeA is complemented by spatial differential attention (SDA) for competitive suppression of nonchange responses and position-aware multihead spectral linear self-attention (SpeLA) for spectral correlation modeling with a favorable accuracy-complexity tradeoff. Experimental results on three public HCD datasets demonstrate competitive and consistent performance, particularly in scenarios where spectral pseudochange causes strong changed/unchanged distribution overlap, and the code is available at https://github.com/WUTCM-Lab/SSDL
item.authors: Bo Zhang;Guirong Feng;Yaxiong Chen;Bingyi Liu;Shili Xiong;Xiaoqiang Lu;

item.title: Radar-Referenced Prior Network for Infrared Iceberg Detection
item.description: In polar waters, ice floes and icebergs pose a threat to navigation safety. Detecting these hazards with shipborne infrared cameras has attracted attention and is being developed. The single sensor is limited in performance under the requirements of extreme cold, fog, and long-range detection, which greatly limits its ability to meet the actual requirements for navigation safety. Introducing spatial position information from navigation radars can assist infrared sensors in achieving precise detection of sea ice targets. In this article, we propose a radar-referenced prior network (RRPNet) and construct an infrared-radar multimodal iceberg target (IRMIT) dataset. For the heterogeneity of infrared and radar data, a dual-source feature extraction (DSFE) encoder is designed to extract the semantic features of infrared and the prior information of radar positions. Then, we propose the detection-reference alignment module (DRAM), which utilizes the cross-modal spatial correlation mechanism to guide the mapping of the position of the radar to the semantic space of infrared. Finally, the multistage feature fusion (MFF) module is designed to enhance the representation ability of ice target features and suppress redundant information across modalities. The experimental results on the IRMIT dataset show that the proposed method effectively improves the performance of infrared ice detection and can achieve effective and robust detection in extremely complex scenarios.
item.authors: Xinyu Ma;Yang Li;Fanglin Chen;Fuhai Guo;Fulin Su;

item.title: Physics-Informed Causal Heterogeneous Change Detection for Geological Disaster Assessment in Steep Mountainous Terrain
item.description: Heterogeneous change detection (CD) aims to detect changes between bi-temporal remote sensing images acquired with different sensors, resolutions, and radiometric properties, a critical capability for geological disaster assessment in steep mountainous terrain. However, existing methods face three intertwined challenges: cross-sensor radiometric inconsistencies that distort feature similarity, terrain-induced pseudo-changes that mask true disaster-changed areas, and error cascades in sequential registration-then-detection pipelines. To overcome these limitations, we propose PhyCDNet, a physics-driven CD framework that fuses the interpretability of radiative transfer physics with causal inference principles. By encoding the functional structure of the radiative transfer equation as learnable network layers and explicitly applying backdoor adjustment to block terrain confounding, we bridge the gap between physical priors and causal representation learning. Our approach translates a physics-constrained optimization model into a structured network comprising a cross-resolution physical manifold alignment (CRMA) module, a physics-constrained causal orthogonal decoupling (PCOD) module, and a continuous feature-flow dynamic alignment (CFDA) module. To further eliminate registration error cascades, CFDA introduces terrain-adaptive deformation constraints, while PCOD leverages orthogonality to expedite causal disentanglement. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate that PhyCDNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on heterogeneous steep-terrain disaster scenarios. We further validate model interpretability through post-hoc radiometric compensation quality (RCQ) and terrain decoupling index (TDI) measurements, confirming that internal feature representations conform to established physical and causal priors. By integrating physics-informed causal constraints with data-driven optimization, PhyCDNet sets a new baseline for reliable and interpretable heterogeneous CD in mountainous regions. Codes are available at our Repository.
item.authors: Zhi Li;Siying Cao;Shun Lv;Zhenming Peng;Yiguang Liu;

item.title: FMC-DETR: Frequency-Decoupled Multidomain Coordination for Aerial-View Object Detection
item.description: Remote sensing object detection (RSOD) is a critical technology for real-world applications such as natural resource monitoring, traffic management, and UAV-based rescue. Detecting tiny objects in high-resolution aerial imagery remains challenging due to weak visual cues and insufficient global context modeling in complex scenes. Existing methods often suffer from delayed contextual interaction and limited nonlinear reasoning, which restrict their ability to effectively refine shallow representations and ultimately lead to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose FMC-DETR, a frequency-decoupled fusion framework for aerial-view object detection. First, we propose the Wavelet Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer (WeKat) backbone, which employs cascaded wavelet transforms to enhance global low-frequency structure perception in shallow features while preserving fine-grained details, and further leverages Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for adaptive nonlinear modeling of multiscale dependencies. Second, we introduce the multidomain feature coordination (MDFC) module, which refines cross-scale fused representations through partial-channel spatial, spectral, and structural coordination, thereby strengthening small-object-related feature responses in cluttered scenes. Finally, we design the compact partial fusion (CPF) module, which performs compact multibranch aggregation with progressive partial refinement to improve feature diversity and multiscale interaction while preserving stable information flow and reducing redundant perturbation. Extensive experiments across multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that FMC-DETR achieves competitive performance and consistently improves over the baseline detector. Code is available at https://github.com/bloomingvision/FMC-DETR
item.authors: Ben Liang;Hongguang Wei;Yuan Liu;Bingwen Qiu;Yihong Wang;Xiubao Sui;Qian Chen;

item.title: First Demonstration of an Onboard Polarimetric Calibration and Ice-Cloud-Based Validation Framework for the Particulate Observing Scanning Polarimeter (POSP)
item.description: Accurate global measurements of atmospheric aerosols and clouds require satellite polarimetric sensors to maintain stable radiometric and polarimetric performance throughout their on-orbit operations. However, monitoring and correcting on-orbit degradation remains a challenge, as most current polarimetric sensors lack active onboard polarimetric calibration capabilities and rely heavily on vicarious calibration methods constrained by atmospheric uncertainties. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of the Particulate Observing Scanning Polarimeter (POSP) onboard the GaoFen-5(02) [GF-5(02)] and DaQi-1 (DQ-1) satellites, which features a unique onboard polarimetric calibration system. Analyzing data from the first one to two years of operation, we identified significant temporal drifts in the calibration coefficients for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) bands (1610 and 2250 nm). These SWIR drifts are consistent with the high thermal sensitivity of the detectors in the on-orbit environment. In addition, the calibration coefficients of the two independent instruments exhibit coherent periodic fluctuations across multiple bands, suggesting the influence of common external thermal and radiative conditions. To independently validate the onboard calibration updates, high-altitude ice clouds observed at scattering angles larger than 170° were used as approximately unpolarized natural References. The validation results demonstrate that the dynamically updated onboard calibration coefficients substantially improve the SWIR polarimetric accuracy. After calibration, the median degree of linear polarization (DoLP) residuals of the SWIR bands agree with the simulated intrinsic ice-cloud DoLP to within one standard deviation of the simulated ensemble. The daily DoLP time series further confirm that the upward drift in the SWIR bands is effectively removed after calibration. Moreover, the validation results reveal a clear latitude dependence: mid-to-high-latitude ice clouds provide more stable and lower uncertainty references than low-latitude ice clouds, which exhibit noticeable seasonal DoLP increases. Overall, this study provides the first on-orbit evaluation of an active onboard polarimetric calibration system, quantifies SWIR-band calibration drifts and cross-platform periodic variations, validates the onboard updates with large scattering angle ice clouds, and establishes a transferable calibration and validation (Cal/Val) framework for future spaceborne polarimetric missions.

item.title: Intelligent Pre-Stack Common Offset Gather Denoising With Post-stack Structure Guidance
item.description: Seismic imaging is primarily used for subsurface exploration. However, the raw imaging results are often severely contaminated by various noises. To eliminate the influence of noises, various seismic denoising algorithms have been developed. Recently, deep-learning-based seismic denoising has been extensively investigated and has demonstrated significant potential. Nevertheless, most of them take only the noisy seismic image as input and directly produce the denoising output. For Pre-stack imaging gathers with extremely strong noise interference, it becomes highly challenging to discern the true structure of effective signals from the noisy input alone. This can lead denoising networks to misinterpret high-amplitude structured noise as genuine signal components, resulting in erroneous restoration. This study focuses on the Pre-stack common offset gather (COG) denoising task and proposes the prior-guided denoising (PGD) algorithm to address this challenge. The proposed PGD algorithm leverages the corresponding stacked image as a structural prior, automatically extracting guidance information to inform the denoising inference for each offset. The advantages of the proposed PGD algorithm over existing algorithms are validated through both synthetic experiments and field data applications. Field application results demonstrate that, by utilizing the stacked image as structural guidance, the PGD algorithm can restore clean single-offset images comparable in quality to Post-stack images. This not only delivers high-fidelity data for subsequent amplitude variation with offset (AVO) analysis but also enables fine-scale interpretation based on Pre-stack imaging gathers.
